fichas.title: Church seating and pew arrangements
fichas.summary: Guidance on church seating layouts, aisle widths, seat and standing-place space requirements, and the use of a central aisle for processions and weddings. Pews may include kneelers; wider churches may require more aisles.
uses: providing circulation for weddings and processions

The layout and form of seating is of great importance for the
dimensions and effect of the space, quality of hearing and view.
In smaller churches (chapels}, an aisle of 1.00 m width is sufficient
---7
with pews containing 6-10 seats, or a central aisle of 1.60 rn
width with seating both sides as ---7 e.
Because of possibly noticeable cold emanating from the external
walls, two side aisles with pews in between ---7 0 containing 12-18
seats is normal.
Wider churches will have correspondingly more aisles. The total
space requirement for each seat is therefore approx 0.63-1.0 rn 2 •
For standing places, 0.25-0.35 m2 each is sufficient; for these a
large part of the aisles, particularly in front of the back wall, is
occupied. The width of the exit doors and steps must comply with
the Places of Assembly Regulations.
A central aisle on the altar axis is often desired for weddings,
processions etc.

Confessional ---7 G)
Three-compartment enclosed booth made of wood, in the central
part of which the Catholic priest sits to hear confession. The
person confessing speaks to the Catholic priest through one of
the two side compartments through a grille of approx. 30 x 40 em.
The lower edge of the opening should be approx. 1.00 m above
floor level. The confessional should be situated inside the church
at a location which is not too bright. Sufficient ventilation and
extraction should be provided.
Today, a confessional room is possible as an alternative.

Vestry---7 0
The vestry (also known as sacristy) is a side room in the church
for the clergy, vestments and equipment for the service. It is best
placed near and to the side of the altar.

fichas.title: Confessional
fichas.summary: A three-compartment enclosed wooden booth places the priest in the central compartment. The person confessing uses one of the two side compartments and speaks through a grille. The confessional should not be in an overly bright location, and ventilation and extraction should be provided. A confessional room is noted as an alternative.

fichas.title: Vestry
fichas.summary: The vestry, also called the sacristy, is a church side room for clergy, vestments, and service equipment. It is best located near and to the side of the altar. The example plan identifies the main room, sexton, vestibule, WC, entrance hall, and access routes.
spaces: main room for robes and altar hangings

fichas.title: Church building shared by two denominations
fichas.summary: A church plan demonstrates shared use by two denominations. Movable partitions create a common space in a double church in Freiburg; the drawings show arrangements for Catholic and Protestant congregations and associated chapel and parish spaces.
uses: sharing church space between two denominations
creating a common space with movable partitions
